title: Binary tree level order traversal
summary: Visit a treehouse one floor at a time: everyone on this floor, then everyone they point to on the floor below.
goal: List the treehouse floor by floor, left to right

examples.label: Three floors
examples.explanation: Floors from the top: 3; then 9 and 20; then 15 and 7.

ladder.name: Collect one floor at a time
ladder.idea: For depth 0, 1, 2, … walk the whole tree collecting the nodes at that depth, until a depth has none.

ladder.name: A queue, one floor at a time
ladder.idea: Keep a queue of nodes on the current floor. Take exactly that many from the front, record them, and add their children for the next floor.
ladder.insight: Children of one floor are exactly the next floor, in left-to-right order. A first-in, first-out queue keeps them in that order, so one pass is enough.

transfer.problem: Print an organisation chart level by level: the CEO, then everyone reporting to the CEO, and so on.
transfer.explanation: Each level is the reports of the previous level, so a queue processed one level at a time gives the order.

selfCheck: Uses a queue, not a stack.
Processes exactly the nodes of the current floor before the next.
Adds left children before right children.
Returns an empty list for an empty tree.
